w: A non-profit café set inside St Mary Aldermary, one of the City's oldest church sites, rebuilt by Christopher Wren after the Great Fire with an unusually intact Gothic fan-vaulted ceiling. Tables sit among the pews under stained glass while the City rushes past outside -- speciality coffee and home baking in a working church repurposed as a genuine pocket of calm.
_facts: Located inside St Mary Aldermary church, Watling Street, City of London EC4M 9BW
St Mary Aldermary was rebuilt by Christopher Wren after the 1666 Great Fire, keeping an earlier Gothic fan-vault design
Run as a non-profit social enterprise café inside the working church
Proceeds support the church's community and charitable work

s: a seasonal canalside café, tables inches from the Regent's Canal
w: A tiny, seasonal cafe (roughly March to November) strung along the Regent's Canal towpath, with a handful of tables set right at the water's edge. The menu changes with what's good that week, the coffee is taken seriously, and the whole thing runs on an unhurried, waterside rhythm that's made it a long-standing favourite among chefs and writers rather than a tourist stop.
_facts: Located on the Regent's Canal towpath at De Beauvoir Crescent, Haggerston/De Beauvoir, London N1 5SB
Open seasonally, roughly March to November
Small, simple seating directly on the canal towpath
Known for a frequently changing, produce-driven menu
